scope: Career-interest and behavior evidence only. Not a clinical or psychometric evaluation.

observations.label: Broad self-directed curiosity
observations.evidence: Personal-interest topics span history, philosophy, monetary systems, technology and learning.
observations.interpretation: May value work with intellectual variety; cannot establish expertise in every topic.

observations.label: Physical persistence
observations.evidence: The website reports a Muay Thai fight, BJJ competition and strength milestones.
observations.interpretation: Direct evidence of participation and follow-through, not proof of coaching ability.

observations.label: Independent product initiative
observations.evidence: The business account describes identifying a niche, researching demand and developing prototypes.
observations.interpretation: Suggests entrepreneurial initiative, not evidence of profitability or scalability.

observations.label: Book and artifact interest
observations.evidence: The site maintains a personal library and reflects on the material value of physical books.
observations.interpretation: Supports rare-book and heritage fields as experiments, not professional competence.

observations.label: Practical craft exploration
observations.evidence: The lifetime-goals section mentions gardening, woodworking, welding and other practical activities.
observations.interpretation: Expressed aspiration, not necessarily demonstrated experience or long-shift preference.

observations.label: Preference for independent control
observations.evidence: The site and linked product project are self-initiated and personally curated.
observations.interpretation: Independence may matter, but tolerance for financial risk and solitude is unknown.

unknowns: Minimum acceptable annual income and financial runway
Enjoyment of teaching and speaking to unfamiliar groups
Actual preference for manual work versus history-related subject matter
Tolerance for irregular income, weekends and weather exposure
Ideal level of independence, teamwork and administration
principles: Treat a stated interest as a hypothesis, not proof of job fit.
Prefer actual shifts and shadowing over another personality questionnaire.
Compare daily tasks rather than impressive job titles.
Do not infer mental health, ideology, diagnoses or standardized scores from a personal website.
